title: Spark's emergency lane is distinguished by permission to reopen the terms of existing positions
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.7.2.5.5 sets the trigger and the powers: "if market conditions or other factors create an **immediate and severe risk of capital impairment**, Spark and Arkis are empowered to implement immediate changes to risk parameters and configuration," including "preventing new loans or draws on existing loans, **adjusting risk parameters of existing positions including increasing margin requirements or haircuts**, demanding immediate repayment, up to and including liquidating high risk positions." A.6.1.1.1.3.8.2.5.5 grants a narrower version for offchain lending — parameters, draw prevention and accelerated repayment, but no unilateral liquidation power.

Read against the non-emergency clause, the difference is not speed but *retroactivity*. Non-emergency updates respect the agreed loan duration; emergency powers reach into live positions and change the terms under which they are margined. That is the line the emergency declaration buys the right to cross.

Defining it this way is unusually precise. Most emergency provisions are written as "may take any necessary action," which is unbounded and therefore untrustworthy. Here the powers are enumerated and escalate in a stated order — stop new exposure, tighten existing exposure, demand repayment, liquidate — so a counterparty can price the worst case and an observer can judge whether the response was proportionate.

The cost is that the trigger is self-assessed. "Immediate and severe risk of capital impairment" has no threshold, no oracle, and no external adjudicator, and for Arkis the power is held jointly by Spark and by the counterparty operating the margin engine. The narrower offchain grant is the tell: where a third-party collateral agent holds the liquidation function, Spark's emergency powers stop short of it.

It is also worth noting what this is *not*. These are product-level powers inside two lending programs. Spark's ecosystem-level and Agent-level emergency response protocols (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.5, .1.6) remain unwritten.
description: Where non-emergency updates only bind new business, an immediate and severe risk of capital impairment authorizes raising margin and haircuts on live positions, demanding repayment, and liquidating.
